DocsHome.title: Connex documentation
DocsHome.lead: Connex is a relationship-intelligence CRM: it scores how warm each relationship is, predicts when one is cooling, and surfaces the warmest path to any introduction. These docs walk every capability, from the big fundamentals down to the small interface details.

DocsGettingStarted.title: Getting started
DocsGettingStarted.description: What Connex is, how workspaces and tenancy work, and how to find your way around.
DocsGettingStarted.lead: Start here. These pages cover the mental model behind Connex and the fundamentals every other section builds on.

what-is-connex.title: What is Connex
what-is-connex.description: The relationship-intelligence CRM and the ideas that make it different.

text: Connex is a multi-tenant CRM built around one idea: your relationships have a temperature, and that temperature changes over time. Instead of a static list of contacts, Connex continuously scores how warm each relationship is, warns you when one is cooling, and shows you the warmest path to reach anyone.
Everything in the product is tenant-scoped and permission-aware. What you see, edit, and share is always bounded by your workspace and your role within it.

items.title: Warmth scoring
items.description: Every relationship carries a temperature score derived from recency, frequency, and depth of interaction.

items.title: Decay prediction
items.description: Connex forecasts when a warm relationship is about to cool so you can act before it does.

items.title: Warm-intro paths
items.description: Reverse-introduction search finds the strongest chain of people who can connect you to a target.

items.title: Employment history
items.description: People carry their job history, so a contact who changes companies keeps their relationship context.

blocks.title: Read in any order

workspaces-and-tenancy.title: Workspaces and tenancy
workspaces-and-tenancy.description: How multi-tenant isolation, workspace switching, and membership work.

blocks.text: A workspace is your tenant. Every record, file, tag, and setting belongs to exactly one workspace, and Connex enforces that boundary on every request. You can belong to more than one workspace and switch between them without logging out.

items.title: Open the workspace switcher
items.description: It sits at the top of the sidebar, showing your current workspace.

items.title: Pick another workspace
items.description: Your active tenant changes immediately and the whole app re-scopes to it.

items.title: Stay oriented
items.description: Your selection is remembered, so you land back in the same workspace next time.

blocks.title: Isolation is absolute
blocks.body: Data never crosses workspaces. An invitation or a shared record is the only way someone in another tenant sees anything you own.

navigating-connex.title: Navigating Connex
navigating-connex.description: The sidebar, global search, breadcrumbs, and how the app is laid out.

blocks.text: The left sidebar groups the app into Overview, Records, Activity, Library, and Team. The header carries global search and your workspace context. Most detail pages offer a back button to their list.

items.action: Dismiss the open menu or dialog

core-concepts.description: Records, relationships, signals, and the shared table mechanics.

blocks.text: A few concepts recur throughout Connex. Learning them once makes every other section easier to read.

blocks.title: Vocabulary
rows: A company, contact, deal, or pipeline you track.
An interaction that feeds a relationship's warmth.
A saved, rule-based slice of your records.
A requested warm connection routed through a mutual contact.

items.question: Is my data shared across workspaces?
items.answer: No. Every record is scoped to one workspace and never leaks to another tenant.

items.question: Do I need to score relationships manually?
items.answer: No. Warmth is computed automatically from the signals Connex already tracks.

DocsDashboard.title: Dashboard & home
DocsDashboard.description: Your personalized home: greeting, at-a-glance metrics, and what needs attention.
DocsDashboard.lead: The dashboard is the first thing you see. It summarizes your workspace and points you at what is urgent.

home-dashboard.title: The home dashboard
home-dashboard.description: Greeting, overview cards, cooling relationships, tasks, and recent moves.

text: The dashboard is your home in Connex. It opens with a greeting that uses your first name and changes with the time of day: good morning through the morning, good afternoon, good evening, and a 'working late' note after 9pm. Beside it you see today's date and a short status line that tells you whether anything needs attention.

That status line is contextual. If you have overdue tasks it turns red and shows the count. If work is simply coming up this week, deals closing, activities planned, or tasks due, it shows a calm summary instead. When nothing is pressing, it says so. The whole page loads its data in parallel, so a skeleton layout stands in for a moment while everything arrives.

items.title: Four core counts
items.description: Companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines each get a card showing the current total for your workspace.

items.title: Everything is a link
items.description: Each card opens the matching records page, and nearly every widget row links straight to the record or detail view behind it.

items.title: Context under the number
items.description: Some cards add a short line below the count, such as how many companies you gained since last week or what your last deal closed for.

blocks.title: Motion, numbers, and accessibility
body: Metric numbers count up from zero over about three quarters of a second, and the cards fade and lift into place one after another. Hovering a card lifts it slightly and nudges its arrow.

All numbers use fixed-width digits so values never shift the layout as they change, and colour follows the design tokens: overdue items in red, temperature pills in their warmth colour. If you have reduced motion enabled in your system, every animation is skipped and content appears at once.

items.title: Pipeline trend
items.description: An area chart plots twelve months of pipeline, with five months of history and the rest as forecast. Toggle between realized revenue from closed deals and projected revenue from open deals; the active metric is highlighted.

items.title: Profit and projections
items.description: Hover either metric to see how it is calculated: profit is revenue already realized from closed deals, projections are the forecast value of open deals by expected close date.

items.title: Multiple currencies
items.description: If your deals span currencies, a selector lets you choose which one to view. It defaults to your most common currency and shows how many deals sit in each.

items.title: Task summary
items.description: See your open task count, an overdue badge, and a 'due this week' line, plus up to four upcoming tasks with their due dates, or 'No date' if unscheduled.

items.title: Finish tasks in place
items.description: Tick a task off straight from the dashboard. The change is instant and a toast offers a one-click undo if you change your mind.

items.title: Overdue stands out
items.description: Past-due tasks show in red with heavier weight, while tasks still in hand show their dates in muted grey.

items.title: Computed from your signals
items.description: These insights read Connex's relationship temperature: the warmth band, whether it is rising or cooling, days since your last touch, and a predicted cold date.

items.title: Cooling relationships
items.description: Contacts that were once warm but have gone quiet, sorted with the most dormant first. Each shows their company, temperature band (hot, warm, cool, or cold), and how many days until the relationship is predicted to go cold.

items.title: One-click follow-up
items.description: Schedule a follow-up before a contact goes cold without leaving the page. The task is assigned to you and links the contact.

items.title: Recently moved
items.description: Contacts who changed companies, detected from their employment history, showing their previous and new company and the date they moved.

items.title: Introduction opportunities
items.description: Up to four suggestions of people you could introduce to each other, with the reason: a shared company or a count of mutual connections.

items.title: Recent files
items.description: The six most recently added files with their type, upload date, and either their linked entity or size. The footer totals your file count and storage used, and each row opens the file in the Files hub.

items.title: Recent activity
items.description: A single reverse-chronological feed that merges tasks, activities, and notes, showing who did what and the records involved. The dashboard shows the latest eight, with a link to the full feed.

items.title: Quick create
items.description: A floating New button in the sidebar, available anywhere in the app, opens New task and New note without leaving your current page.

items.title: New task
items.description: A short dialog takes a description and an optional due date, assigns the task to you, and offers a View action in the success toast.

items.title: New note
items.description: A dialog takes your note content and files it, again with a View action to jump to the notes hub.

items.question: Why does a widget show a message instead of a list?
items.answer: When there is no data yet, cooling relationships, recent moves, introductions, files, and recent activity each show a short explanation rather than empty space.

items.question: How are the section headings and links organised?
items.answer: Every section has an uppercase label and, where it helps, a right-aligned action such as View all or View map that opens the full view. Almost every row links deep into the underlying record.

items.question: What happens when an action fails?
items.answer: Creating a task or note, completing a task, and scheduling a follow-up all update optimistically. If the request fails, the change rolls back and a dismissible error toast explains why. Buttons disable and show a spinner while a request is in flight.

items.question: How is follow-up timing chosen?
items.answer: If a contact has a predicted cold date, the follow-up is scheduled five days before it; otherwise it defaults to three days out, and never earlier than tomorrow. Once scheduled, the calendar icon becomes a check in a warm colour.

items.question: Does the dashboard adapt to my language and screen?
items.answer: All text and dates follow your language, English or Japanese, with full dates on wider screens and abbreviated ones when space is tight. The grid reflows from two to four columns for the cards and from one to two columns for the wider sections, lists scroll within their cards when they overflow, and long names truncate with an ellipsis.

items.question: How does it stay fast?
items.answer: The dashboard fetches every data source at once rather than one at a time, reads a cached copy of your relationship temperatures on first load, and computes things like overdue tasks and deals closing this week on the spot from that data.

DocsRecords.title: Records
DocsRecords.description: Companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines, plus the shared table mechanics they all use.
DocsRecords.lead: Records are the people and organizations you track. They share a common table, filtering, and detail-page experience.

records-overview.title: Records overview
records-overview.description: How the four record types relate and what they have in common.

text: Records are the people and organizations you track in Connex. There are four record types: companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines. They share one table-and-grid engine, one detail-page layout, and one set of controls for search, filtering, tags, custom fields, attachments, and sharing, so learning one makes the others familiar.
Every record lives inside a single workspace. Connex enforces that boundary on every request, and your role governs what you can view, edit, and delete.

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Organizations, their people, deals, custom fields, and timeline.

blocks.text: A company is an organization you track. Connex lists every company in your workspace in a searchable, paginated view you can display as cards or as a sortable table, with full-text search across name, website, industry, phone, and address. Open any company to see its full profile.

items.title: Open the new company dialog
items.description: Enter the name, website, industry, phone, and address. Upload a logo by drag-and-drop or file picker; without one, Connex shows a lettered avatar.

items.title: Let the helpers guide you
items.description: The industry field suggests values already used in your workspace, and the website field adds http:// or https:// for you when you leave it.

items.title: Stage contacts to add with it
items.description: Queue one or more people, each with a name, title, email, and optional photo, to be created right after the company is saved.

items.title: Save
items.description: The company is created, then the staged contacts. If some contacts fail, Connex reports a partial success.

blocks.title: Duplicate websites are caught
blocks.body: If a website matches an existing company (protocol and www stripped, lowercased), a warning badge links you to that company and blocks the save, so you do not create a second record for the same domain.

items.title: Contacts grid
items.description: Every person at the company, with an empty state and a button to add one pre-scoped to the company.

items.title: Deals pipeline
items.description: A Pipeline card groups the company's deals by stage, with names, values, and statuses.

items.title: Revenue tiles
items.description: Closed and projected revenue in the company's dominant currency, formatted compactly.

items.title: Engagement sparkline
items.description: A 12-week area chart of weekly interactions, with a per-week breakdown on hover.

items.title: Interaction timeline
items.description: Every activity, note, and task on the company or its contacts, in chronological order.

items.title: Team interactions
items.description: Avatars of teammates who have logged anything with the company; hover for names, click to open a profile.

items.title: Custom fields
items.description: Set and edit workspace-defined fields directly on the profile.

items.title: Attachments
items.description: Upload and download files against the company.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Add colored tags on the profile, or to many companies at once.

items.title: Quick actions
items.description: Create a new contact or deal from the actions menu, pre-scoped to this company.

items.title: Share
items.description: Share a company with workspace members; only companies your workspace owns can be shared.

items.title: View in map
items.description: Open the overview map focused on this company and its contacts.

blocks.title: Jump to industry peers
blocks.body: The industry shown on a company profile is a link. Click it to filter the companies list to everyone in the same industry.

items.question: How is a company's warmth calculated?
items.answer: It is computed server-side from the recency and frequency of interactions with the company's contacts, and it decays on a fixed half-life, so older touches count for less. You can sort the table by it.

items.question: Can I edit or delete several companies at once?
items.answer: Yes. Select multiple companies to quick-edit shared fields, or delete them in one confirmed, transactional action. Results report per-record success and failure.

items.question: Are my view preferences remembered?
items.answer: Grid-versus-table choice, sort order, and search are saved to your browser, so they survive a refresh. You can also name and reuse full filter setups as saved views, including smart segments built from AND/OR predicates.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: People, their employment history, warmth, and connections.

blocks.text: A contact is a person you know. Each has a profile with name, email, phone, title, company, tags, and a photo, plus the relationship context Connex is built around: employment history, a warmth score, connections into your network, and a full activity timeline.

items.title: Open the new contact dialog
items.description: The name field is focused for you. Name is required; email, phone, title, and company are optional.

items.title: Add a photo
items.description: Upload a profile picture, or let Connex show color-tinted initials in its place.

items.title: Save
items.description: A brief success animation confirms the create, then the dialog closes.

items.title: Edit later, one or many
items.description: Edit a single contact, or quick-edit name, email, phone, and title across several selected contacts at once. Deleting one or many asks for confirmation.

items.title: Identity
items.description: Name, title, company, email, phone, and dates in a clean readonly layout, with an avatar that falls back to initials.

items.title: Employment history
items.description: An automatic record of every company worked for, with titles and dates; the current role is marked and updates when the company changes.

items.title: Warmth
items.description: A color-coded temperature pill with a numeric score and days until decay.

items.title: Connections
items.description: Typed relationships (knows, colleague, former colleague, friend) and the shortest warm-introduction path to the contact.

items.title: Activity timeline
items.description: Activities, notes, and tasks in one dated feed, showing who created each item.

items.title: Deals
items.description: The deals the contact is linked to, with status, name, and value.

items.title: Log activity
items.description: Record a call, email, meeting, note, or other, with a subject, notes, and an optional deal.

items.title: Notes and tasks
items.description: Write a note, or create a task with an assignee and due date, optionally tied to a deal.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Add colored tags on the contact, or to many contacts at once.

items.title: Custom fields
items.description: Edit workspace-defined fields in place, or in bulk from quick edit.

items.title: Attachments
items.description: Store files against the contact, from documents to business cards.

items.title: Stats and interactions
items.description: Summary cards count activities, open tasks, and deals; avatars show which teammates have engaged.

blocks.title: Initials get a consistent color
blocks.body: A contact without a photo shows lettered initials tinted from one of nine colors, chosen deterministically from a hash of the name, so the same person always gets the same color.

blocks.title: Card quick actions
rows: Opens a mailto: link to the contact's address.
Copies the phone number and confirms with a toast.
Reassigns or clears the company, recording the move in employment history.
Opens the overview map with the contact focused.
Shares the contact with members; only contacts your workspace owns can be shared.

items.question: Does employment history update itself?
items.answer: Yes. When you create a contact or change their company, single or in bulk, Connex records the transition automatically and marks the current role.

items.question: Can I find people who just changed jobs?
items.answer: Connex tracks contacts who moved companies in the last 90 days, up to the 20 most recent, as a recently moved feed.

items.question: What does the warm-introduction path show?
items.answer: It is the shortest chain of people you know that reaches a given contact, and it tells you when someone is directly known or currently unreachable.

deals-and-pipelines.title: Deals & pipelines
deals-and-pipelines.description: Opportunities moving through stages, and the pipelines that shape them.

blocks.text: A deal is an opportunity moving through a pipeline. It carries a name, value, currency, company, owner, and stage, and ends in an outcome of won or lost. A pipeline is the ordered set of stages a deal passes through. Both are scoped to your workspace and gated by permissions.

items.title: Pipeline browser
items.description: See every pipeline as a collapsible card showing stage count, deal count, related users, and stage names.

items.title: Create and edit
items.description: Name a pipeline and give it stages; rename, reorder, retype, or remove stages inline at any time.

items.title: Stage kinds
items.description: Each stage is normal, won, or lost. Won and lost are terminal: a deal reaching one auto-closes with that outcome.

items.title: Progress view
items.description: A deal's detail page shows a horizontal timeline of its stages, the current one highlighted, with a schedule status overlaid.

blocks.title: Stage rules Connex enforces
body: A pipeline may have at most one won stage and one lost stage.
Stage names must be unique within a pipeline, case-insensitively.
A deal cannot move to a stage in a different pipeline.
Reopening a closed deal that sits on a terminal stage moves it back to the last normal stage, and Connex keeps the close timestamp and outcome consistent automatically.

items.title: Create and quick-edit
items.description: Create a deal with inline validation; quick-edit one or many, stepping through a batch one deal at a time.

items.title: Team
items.description: Assign one owner and any number of collaborators; a user is one or the other, never both.

items.title: People
items.description: Link contacts to the deal, each with an optional role such as Decision Maker.

items.title: Tags and custom fields
items.description: Categorize with colored tags and fill workspace-defined custom fields.

items.title: Timeline
items.description: Activities, notes, tasks, and system events such as stage changes and closes, in one feed.

items.title: Attachments
items.description: Store proposals, contracts, and other files on the deal.

blocks.text: Mark a deal won or lost to record its outcome, an optional close reason, and the actual value realized; the close date is stamped for you. Reopening clears the outcome. For closed deals, Connex shows the variance between projected and actual value as a percentage, and status pills read open, won, or lost at a glance. Expected and actual close dates drive a schedule status of on time, behind, ahead, or overdue.

items.title: Revenue forecast
items.description: A chart pairing six months of history with six months ahead, projected value against actual closed revenue by month.

items.title: Stage and pipeline mix
items.description: Pie charts of deal count and revenue across stages and pipelines, open and closed shown at different opacity.

items.title: Top deals
items.description: Your highest-value open deals, surfaced on the main dashboard.

items.title: Engagement
items.description: A 12-week sparkline and activity breakdown on each deal to gauge momentum.

items.question: How does multi-currency work?
items.answer: Every deal has a three-character currency code. Values format with the right symbol and separators, you can filter by currency, and charts aggregate only the dominant or selected currency.

items.question: What happens when I move a deal to a won or lost stage?
items.answer: It closes automatically with that outcome. If the deal was already closed, its outcome updates to match the stage.

items.question: Which permissions do deals need?
items.answer: Creating needs DEAL_CREATE, editing, closing, or reopening needs DEAL_UPDATE, deleting needs DEAL_DELETE, and managing pipelines needs PIPELINE_MANAGE. Deletions are confirmed, and both deals and pipelines keep an audit trail.

table-and-grid.title: Table & grid mechanics
table-and-grid.description: Sorting, column controls, selection, and bulk actions shared across records.

blocks.text: Companies, contacts, deals, and pipelines all render through the same table-and-grid engine, so whatever you learn here applies everywhere records are listed. You can display any list as cards or as a table, and Connex remembers your choice per record type in both the browser and the URL.

items.title: Card grid
items.description: A responsive multi-column grid of clickable, selectable cards, each with an avatar, summary, and action menu.

items.title: Data table
items.description: A dense, horizontally scrollable table with sortable columns and a checkbox column.

items.title: Sticky and frozen
items.description: The header stays put as you scroll down, and the checkbox, avatar, and first named column stay fixed as you scroll sideways.

items.title: Persistent choice
items.description: Your grid-or-table preference, sort order, and search persist across reloads.

items.title: Column sorting
items.description: Click a sortable header to sort ascending, click again for descending; a chevron marks the active column.

items.title: Full-text search
items.description: Search across the record's key fields; input is debounced and reflected in the URL.

items.title: Filter menu
items.description: Faceted filters aggregated from your data; choices within a facet are OR'd, facets are AND'd, with an active count badge.

items.title: Filter chips
items.description: Active filters and the search query appear as removable chips above the table.

items.title: Saved views
items.description: Name a full setup of filters, sort, search, and segments; a dot marks when the current view is unsaved.

items.title: Smart segments
items.description: Combine graph-aware predicates like warm intro or open deal with field comparisons, using ALL or ANY logic.

items.title: Select rows
items.description: Tick individual checkboxes, or the header checkbox to select the whole page. The header shows an indeterminate state for partial selections.

items.title: Extend to everything matching
items.description: When the page is fully selected, Connex offers to select every record matching your current filters and search across all pages.

items.title: Use the selection bar
items.description: A floating bar shows the selected count and the available bulk actions.

items.title: Apply the action
items.description: Add or remove a tag, assign an owner or change stage for deals, quick-edit shared fields, or delete. Results report per-record success and failure.

items.title: Quick edit sheet
items.description: A side sheet edits shared fields across the selection, saved in parallel with a success animation.

items.title: Inline custom fields
items.description: Edit custom field cells in place; double-click or Enter to edit, with text, number, date, URL, select, and boolean types.

items.title: Custom field columns
items.description: Admins add, configure, or delete custom field columns per record type.

items.title: Copyable cells
items.description: Email, phone, website, company, and address cells copy to the clipboard on click, confirmed by a toast.

items.title: Import and export
items.description: Bring records in from CSV or Excel and export the current view to CSV.

items.title: Open a record
items.description: Click a row, or a card, to open its detail page; clicks on checkboxes, copy cells, and menus do not navigate.

blocks.title: Navigating wide tables
blocks.body: When a table has more columns than fit, gradient overlays at the edges hint there is more to see, and you can drag to scroll horizontally with the middle mouse button or by dragging the header row. Frozen columns keep names in view the whole way across.

items.question: How many records per page?
items.answer: Tables paginate server-side at 25 by default, adjustable to 10, 25, 50, or 100. A 'Showing X to Y of Z' line keeps you oriented, and changing filters, sort, or search returns you to page one.

items.question: Do edits show immediately?
items.answer: Yes. Quick edits, custom field changes, and bulk actions update the UI optimistically and revert with a toast if the server rejects them.

items.question: Does selection survive paging?
items.answer: Yes. Your selection is tracked across pagination and sorting within the same filtered result set, and a select-all-matching flow fetches every matching record's id from the server.

items.question: What do I see while loading or with no results?
items.answer: While data loads you get skeleton placeholders, and when nothing matches you get a centered empty state with a Clear Filters button when filters are active.

DocsRelationshipIntelligence.title: Relationship intelligence
DocsRelationshipIntelligence.description: Warmth scoring, decay prediction, connections, and employment history: the heart of Connex.
DocsRelationshipIntelligence.lead: This is what sets Connex apart. Relationships are scored, watched for decay, and mapped into a graph you can traverse.

warmth-and-temperature.title: Warmth & temperature
warmth-and-temperature.description: How relationship temperature is scored and what the bands mean.

blocks.text: Every relationship in Connex carries a temperature. It rises with recent, frequent, meaningful contact and falls as interactions thin out. The score rolls up into four readable bands so you can scan a list and know where each relationship stands.

items.label: Hot
items.description: Active, frequent, recent contact. The relationship is thriving.

items.label: Warm
items.description: Healthy and current, with steady but less frequent touchpoints.

items.label: Cool
items.description: Fading. Contact has slowed and the relationship needs attention.

items.label: Cold
items.description: Dormant. Little or no recent interaction to draw on.

blocks.title: Scores are computed, not entered
blocks.body: You never set a temperature by hand. It is derived from the signals Connex already tracks: notes, activities, meetings, and messages.

decay-and-signals.title: Decay & signals
decay-and-signals.description: How Connex predicts cooling relationships and what feeds the score.

blocks.text: Warmth decays over time. Connex models that decay and flags relationships that are about to slip a band, so you can reach out before they cool. The dashboard surfaces these as cooling relationships.

items.title: Notes
items.description: Written context you log against a record.

items.title: Activities
items.description: Calls, meetings, and touchpoints you record.

items.title: Tasks
items.description: Completed follow-ups tied to a relationship.

items.title: Calendar events
items.description: Meetings connected to the people involved.

blocks.title: Quiet days are counted
blocks.body: A relationship's cooling estimate reflects how many days it has been quiet, not just the last interaction type, so a long gap after many touchpoints still triggers a warning.

connections-and-employment.title: Connections & employment
connections-and-employment.description: The relationship graph and how job history keeps context when people move.

blocks.text: People are connected to companies through employment history. When someone changes jobs, their relationships and context travel with them, and the connection graph updates to reflect where they are now.

items.title: Warm-intro paths
items.description: Traverse the connection graph to find the strongest route to a target.

items.title: Relationship map
items.description: See the graph visually and explore how people connect.

DocsOverviewSuite.title: Overview suite
DocsOverviewSuite.description: Analytics, the relationship map, calendar, introductions, and warm-intro paths.
DocsOverviewSuite.lead: The overview suite turns your records into insight: charts, a live relationship graph, and tools for engineering introductions.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Revenue trends, pipeline value, win rates, and team leaderboards.

blocks.text: The analytics dashboard pulls your deals, pipelines, and activity into one screen for sales intelligence and performance tracking: revenue trends, pipeline health, win rates, team activity, and deal aging. It is one of the four tabs in the overview suite, alongside the map, calendar, and introductions. Every calculation on the page uses a single timestamp captured when the page loads, so the numbers stay consistent with each other, and the layout adapts from a single stacked column on mobile up to the full multi-panel grid on larger screens.

items.title: Time range
items.description: Switch between 30 days, 90 days, and 12 months. Every KPI, chart, and trend recalculates for the range you pick.

items.title: Currency
items.description: When deals span several currencies, choose which one the whole dashboard shows. It defaults to the currency with the most deals; single-currency workspaces show it as a badge instead of a selector.

items.title: Won revenue
items.description: Total actual value of deals won in the range, using each deal's final won value rather than its original expected value.

items.title: New pipeline
items.description: Total expected value of every deal opened in the range, whether or not it later closed.

items.title: Win rate
items.description: Share of deals closed in the range that were won (won divided by won plus lost). Deals closed without a win or lose stage are left out.

items.title: Average sales cycle
items.description: Average days from creation to close, counted only for deals won in the range. Lower is better.

blocks.title: Reading the sparklines and deltas
blocks.body: Each KPI carries a 12-bucket sparkline showing its shape over the range, and a delta comparing this range to the previous equal-length one: a green arrow for a good move, red for a bad one. Win rate's delta is in percentage points (pp), not percent. If a change is smaller than 0.5% it shows flat with no arrow, and if there is nothing to compare against the delta reads 'No prior data' rather than a misleading number.

items.title: Revenue trend
items.description: Won revenue by month against projected pipeline, extending up to 12 months forward from deals' expected close dates. An open-pipeline badge sits by the title, and the hover tooltip shows exact won and projected values.

items.title: Pipeline value
items.description: Pipelines ranked by total value as stacked bars, won in the primary colour and open in a lighter tint. Pipelines with no activity are hidden.

items.title: Stage funnel
items.description: Open deals in a chosen pipeline broken out by stage, each bar sized by value. Won stages are green, lost stages red, and normal stages shade progressively lighter from first to last.

items.title: Win rate donut
items.description: Deals closed in the range, won versus lost by count, with the win rate in the centre and values in the legend.

items.title: Activity volume
items.description: Stacked bars of logged activity by type over time. Only types with at least one entry in the range appear.

items.title: Team leaderboard
items.description: Top five members by 'touches', which counts logged activities, completed tasks, and authored notes equally.

items.title: Deal aging
items.description: Open deals per stage bucketed as Fresh, Active, Aging, and Stalled by how recently they were touched.

items.title: Top deals
items.description: The three biggest open deals and three biggest wins, ranked with gold, silver, and bronze trophies. Each is clickable.

blocks.title: How the numbers are calculated
rows: Uses each deal's actual won value, not the original expected value.
Sum of expected value for deals that are neither won nor lost yet.
Excludes deals closed without an explicit win or lose stage.
Days from creation to close, for won deals only.
Measured from a deal's last update, so active editing keeps it fresh; untouched for 60+ days counts as stalled.
Driven by an explicit won flag and filtered by close date, so a future-dated close is not counted yet and time zones do not skew results.

blocks.title: Formatting and motion
blocks.body: Currency values use compact notation (1k, 1m, 1b) and dates follow your locale, so the same dashboard reads correctly in English or Japanese. Sections fade and slide in with a short staggered delay, bars ease to width over half a second, and the range control springs into place. All of it respects your reduced-motion preference.

items.question: Why does the stage funnel already have a pipeline selected?
items.answer: It auto-picks the first pipeline that has open deals, sorted by open-deal count. Pipelines with no open deals are not selectable.

items.question: What if the workspace has no deals?
items.answer: The dashboard shows a friendly empty state with links to create a deal or set up a pipeline, and individual charts show a 'No data' message rather than breaking.

items.question: Can I drill into the detail?
items.answer: Yes. Pipeline names, team members, and deals are links that jump to their full records. An info icon on each panel explains how that metric is calculated.

relationship-map.title: Relationship map
relationship-map.description: An interactive graph of people, companies, and how they connect.

blocks.text: The relationship map is an interactive network of your organisation, your team, the companies you work with, and their contacts, with the connections between them drawn as edges. It centres on your organisation and lets you explore deals, revenue, and engagement by expanding the nodes you care about.

items.title: Your organisation
items.description: A central blue building icon that anchors the graph. It sits fixed at the centre.

items.title: Team members
items.description: Your users, drawn as avatars in the first ring around the organisation.

items.title: Client companies
items.description: The companies you work with, shown with their logos in the second ring.

items.title: Contacts
items.description: People at those companies, shown with profile pictures in the outer ring.

items.title: Expand a node
items.description: Click a company or contact to open a detailed card. Companies show industry, website, phone, deal and people counts, past and projected revenue, and a 12-week engagement sparkline; contacts show title, a clickable email, and phone.

items.title: Hover to trace
items.description: Hovering a node highlights its whole tree, all parents up to the organisation and all contacts below, while dimming everything else.

items.title: Drag to reposition
items.description: Click and drag any node to move it. The force simulation reheats so nodes settle back into a balanced layout.

items.title: Controls
items.description: Bottom-right controls give you zoom in and out, fit-to-view, and a lock to freeze panning. Pan, zoom, and a background grid are on by default.

items.title: Focus on load
items.description: Opening the map with a contact or company in the link expands that node and glides the camera to it; without one, the map fits everything in view.

items.title: Legend
items.description: A toggle in the top-right corner expands into a full reference of node types, connection types, and deal statuses.

items.title: Warmth at a glance
items.description: Nodes carry a temperature tint, hot to cold, via a coloured dot or node colour. Contacts with recent activity get a solid green border; inactive ones get a dashed border.

items.title: Edge meaning
items.description: Solid lines are org membership, gradient lines carry deals, dashed lines are known relationships with no deals, and thin lines link companies to their contacts. Deal edges shade toward green for won, red for lost, or blue for open.

items.title: Deal popover
items.description: Hover an edge that carries deals to see every deal on that relationship with its name and status.

items.title: Company detail
items.description: Expanded company cards show past and projected revenue tiles in the company's main currency, multi-currency aware, plus the rolling engagement sparkline.

items.title: Quick links
items.description: Expanded cards show avatar groups of related employees and team members; click any avatar to jump to that record.

items.title: View the full record
items.description: A chevron in the top-right of an expanded card opens the complete company or contact page.

blocks.title: Performance at scale
blocks.body: Once ten or more companies are on the map, nodes collapse to small coloured shapes (squares for companies, circles for contacts) and bloom into full cards on hover, keeping large graphs legible and fast. Labels crossfade by zoom level and disappear when you zoom far out, and an unhovered node blooms upward to a larger avatar. Node positions are set by a d3 force simulation that settles with a gentle drift over about 700ms. All of the motion respects your reduced-motion preference.

blocks.title: How the map stays fresh
blocks.body: Most of the map's data, companies, contacts, deals, activities, and the rest, is cached by your browser for speed, while relationship temperature is always fetched fresh so warmth stays accurate. Website links on expanded cards open in a new tab and are sanitised so only safe URLs can be followed.

items.description: Turn the same graph into the strongest route to a contact you want to reach.

items.title: Introductions
items.description: Act on the connections you spot by recording and tracking intros.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Your meetings and events tied back to the relationships they involve.

blocks.text: The calendar is a month view that gathers everything happening across your workspace, tasks, activities, deals, and notes, onto the days they fall on. It always draws a full six-week grid, filling in leading and trailing days from the neighbouring months so the layout stays steady no matter which day the month starts on. Days outside the current month are greyed out.

items.title: Tasks
items.description: Shown in the brand colour. Each chip links through to your tasks.

items.title: Activities
items.description: Shown in blue. Chips link to your activity feed.

items.title: Deals
items.description: Shown in amber. Chips link straight to the deal record.

items.title: Notes
items.description: Shown in muted grey. Chips link to the note.

items.title: Move by month
items.description: Step backward and forward with the chevron buttons at the top of the calendar.

items.title: Jump to today
items.description: The Today button smooth-scrolls back to the current month, and today's date is marked with a filled blue circle.

items.title: Ordered by priority
items.description: Within a day, entries sort deals first, then tasks, activities, and notes, so the most important items sit at the top without scrolling.

items.title: Hover for detail
items.description: Hovering a chip shows the full content: a task's description, an activity's subject and type, a deal's name, or a note preview trimmed to 60 characters.

items.title: Click to open
items.description: Every chip is a link. Deals open the exact record; tasks and activities open their feed pages, and notes open with the note in focus.

items.title: Busy days scroll
items.description: When a day holds more entries than fit its cell, the entries scroll within that cell instead of stretching the grid.

blocks.title: How the calendar places entries
blocks.body: Entries are grouped by their date (year-month-day) with no time-of-day precision, so an item lands on its day regardless of the hour. Any entry with an invalid date is quietly skipped rather than shown in the wrong place. Calendar data is fetched fresh on every load, never cached, so what you see always reflects the latest timestamps. Task and activity chips open their feed pages without yet highlighting the specific entry.

introductions.title: Introductions
introductions.description: Request, track, and fulfill warm introductions between contacts.

blocks.text: The introductions page helps you engineer warm connections between people your team already knows. It has two halves: suggested introductions that Connex surfaces for you, and a lineage feed recording every intro your team has made. You can also log an intro by hand.
Each suggestion is a card pairing two contacts with an arrow between them, reading 'introduce A to B'. It shows each person's avatar, name, title, and company, and gives you the context to decide.

items.title: Warmth badges
items.description: A tinted chip by each name shows your relationship temperature with that person, hot to cold, when warmth data is available.

items.title: Reason chips
items.description: Chips explain the connection, such as 'N mutual connections' or 'Shared employer: CompanyName', shown only when they apply.

items.title: Record the intro
items.description: Marks the introduction as made. It creates a connection between the two contacts and adds the pair to your lineage feed.

items.title: Or dismiss it
items.description: Removes a suggestion that does not apply and tells the backend not to surface that pair again.

blocks.title: Instant, reversible actions
blocks.body: Record and Dismiss update the screen immediately, before the server replies: the card fades and pops out at once. If the request fails, the card comes back and an error toast explains why. Each card allows only one action, so a quick double-click cannot record and dismiss the same pair.

blocks.text: The lineage feed lists every introduction your team has made, newest first. Each row shows both contacts with clickable avatars and names, the time since the intro in relative form such as '2 hours ago', who made it, and any note beneath. Until anyone records an intro, the feed shows a placeholder inviting you to connect two contacts.

items.title: Open the dialog
items.description: The 'Log an intro' button opens a dialog for intros you made outside the system or before adopting the feature.

items.title: Pick two contacts
items.description: Use the searchable pickers to choose both people. The second picker excludes the first, so you cannot introduce someone to themselves.

items.title: Add optional context
items.description: Write up to 500 characters on how or why you introduced them. The note is trimmed and stored with the intro.

items.title: Record it
items.description: The button stays disabled until two different contacts are chosen. On success the dialog resets; if it fails it stays open so you can retry.

items.question: How many suggestions load at once?
items.answer: The page requests the top 40 suggestions, and the lineage feed is paginated at 50 entries per page.

items.question: Why did a suggestion disappear before I refreshed?
items.answer: Suggestions are fetched fresh every visit and never cached, so recording or dismissing removes them right away. Lineage is cached to keep the feed fast.

items.question: Is the page available in Japanese?
items.answer: Yes. Every card, dialog, reason label, toast, and empty state is translated, and Japanese text renders in Noto Sans JP.

warm-intro-paths.title: Warm-intro paths
warm-intro-paths.description: Reverse-introduction search for the strongest path to any target.

blocks.text: Warm-intro paths run the introduction engine in reverse: instead of asking who can reach a target, Connex automatically finds pairs of contacts you are positioned to introduce, because your team knows both of them but they do not yet know each other. Each candidate carries a score from 0 to 100 and a short explanation of why the two should connect. Suggestions appear on the Introductions page and as a compact widget on the dashboard showing the top four opportunities.

items.title: Someone you actually know
items.description: Only workspace-owned contacts your team has genuinely engaged qualify, meaning at least one activity, note, or task. Records shared in from another tenant are excluded.

items.title: Not already connected
items.description: Pairs that already share a connection, or that you have previously recorded or dismissed, are filtered out before ranking.

items.title: Warmth on each side
items.description: Every candidate shows both contacts' warmth bands, so introducing two hot contacts reads differently from pairing a hot and a cold one. Warmth feeds the ranking.

items.title: Readable reasons
items.description: Reason chips align with the scoring signals: 'N mutual connections' and 'Shared employer: CompanyName', so you can judge signal quality at a glance.

items.title: Record
items.description: Locks in the intro by creating a 'knows' connection at strength 2 and logging it to lineage. A stronger existing connection is never downgraded, and the pair leaves your suggestions.

items.title: Dismiss
items.description: Suppresses a pair without recording an intro. It is marked dismissed in the database and permanently drops out of the candidate set, steering ranking toward better opportunities.

items.title: Log manually
items.description: Records an intro between any two workspace contacts, even a pair that was never suggested, with an optional note up to 500 characters.

blocks.title: Rules that keep lineage clean
blocks.body: Recording is idempotent: introducing A to B and later B to A upserts a single row, refreshing the note and timestamp rather than duplicating. If a pair is recorded as made and later dismissed, it stays made, dismissals only apply to pairs not yet recorded, so history is never erased. Trying to introduce a contact to themselves is rejected outright as a bad request, and lineage rows are immutable once written.

blocks.title: Who can act
blocks.body: Every operation is scoped to the current workspace, and recording or dismissing requires the person-update permission, so only team members with the right role can act. Contacts from another workspace are rejected at the permission layer, never leaking across tenants.

items.title: Introductions
items.description: The page where these suggestions live, plus the lineage feed and manual logging.

items.title: Relationship map
items.description: See the connection graph these suggestions are drawn from.

DocsActivity.title: Activity
DocsActivity.description: Notes, tasks, activities, and calendar events: the signals behind warmth.
DocsActivity.lead: Activity is where the relationship signal comes from. Everything you log here feeds warmth and keeps history complete.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Freeform context logged against any record, with mentions.

blocks.text: Notes are freeform context you log against your records. Write down what was said, what matters, and what to remember, then link the note to a contact or a deal so the history lives where you need it. Every linked note becomes a signal that feeds relationship warmth.

items.title: Write the content
items.description: The content field is multiline and auto-focuses, so you can start typing straight away. Longer notes are welcome.

items.title: Link it to a record
items.description: Attach the note to a contact and/or a deal to give it context. Linked notes are visible to your whole workspace.

items.title: Save
items.description: The note is recorded against the linked record and appears in the notes view. You can set an author override if you are logging on someone else's behalf.

blocks.title: A note with no link is private
blocks.body: If you create a note without linking it to a contact or deal, it stays private and only you, the author, can see it. Private notes show a lock icon and a Private label. Link the note to a record to share it with the workspace.

items.title: Grid view
items.description: The default. Notes appear as square cards showing the heading, body, linked contact and deal, author, and last-modified date. Hover a card to reveal edit, copy, and delete actions.

items.title: Table view
items.description: A sortable table with Content, Person, Deal, Author, Created, and Updated columns. Click a row to open it for editing.

items.title: Group by person or company
items.description: In grid view, group notes by the linked contact or that contact's company. Unlinked notes fall into a No person or No company section, and each group carries a count badge.

items.title: Search
items.description: Full-text search runs across note content, the linked contact and deal names, and the author's name, using case-insensitive matching.

items.title: Select several
items.description: Tick the checkbox on cards or table rows. A selection bar appears at the bottom with Quick Edit and Delete.

items.title: Quick Edit
items.description: Open every selected note in one side sheet and edit content and links together. Only notes you actually changed are saved.

items.title: Copy content
items.description: Copy a note's full content to your clipboard from the card action menu. A toast confirms the copy.

items.title: Delete
items.description: Remove one or many selected notes at once, with a confirmation step first.

blocks.title: The first line becomes a heading
blocks.body: If a note's content contains a line break, the first line renders as a bold heading and the rest as body text. Single-line notes render as plain text. This lets you build tidy, structured note templates just by adding a newline.

items.question: Who can see my private notes?
items.answer: Only you. A note with no linked contact or deal is visible to its author alone. Link it to a record to share it with the workspace.

items.question: Can I change a note's author after creating it?
items.answer: No. The original author is preserved when you edit a note. Editing changes the content and links, not the authorship.

items.question: What happens if a field is invalid?
items.answer: Validation errors appear inline beneath the field, and the first field with an error is focused. The error clears as soon as you edit that field.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: Follow-ups with due dates, assignment, and completion.

blocks.text: Tasks are follow-ups with a due date, an owner, and a completion state. Assign work to a workspace member, tie it to the contact or deal it concerns, and track it through to done. Task changes publish in real time, so assignees stay up to date without refreshing.

items.title: Describe the work
items.description: A description is required. Keep it short and action-oriented.

items.title: Assign it
items.description: Every task needs an assignee, and the assignee must be a member of the workspace. You cannot create an unassigned task.

items.title: Add a due date and links
items.description: Optionally set a due date and link the task to a contact and/or deal so it shows up in the right context.

blocks.title: Tasks always have an owner
blocks.body: An assignee is required at creation and when editing, and Connex validates that they belong to the workspace. If you have nobody to assign yet, the task lands in the Unassigned queue only when it has no assignee, so plan to assign it before it can be worked.

blocks.title: The six queues
rows: Incomplete tasks whose due date has passed.
Every incomplete task in the workspace.
Tasks that are done, as a flat list.

items.title: Buckets
items.description: Inside the active queues, tasks group into collapsible sections: Overdue, Today, Upcoming, No Date, and Completed, each sorted by due date.

items.title: Due date chips
items.description: Each row shows a tone-coded due date chip: red for overdue, brand color for today, and gray for soon or later. Completed tasks hide the chip.

items.title: Today focus strip
items.description: A dashboard widget with a progress ring of today's done and total, a count of overdue tasks, and how many you completed this week. Each card jumps to its queue.

items.title: Assignee and links
items.description: Rows show the assignee's avatar with their name on hover, plus clickable badges for the linked contact and deal.

blocks.title: Only the assignee can complete a task
blocks.body: Completion is toggled from the circular checkbox on the row. The task marks complete optimistically with a brief linger animation before it commits, but the server enforces that only the assignee may complete their own task. Others can view it, not tick it off.

items.question: How do I find a specific task?
items.answer: Use full-text search across description, linked contact and deal, and assignee name, or narrow the current queue with the dimensional filter by assignee, contact, deal, or company. Selections are OR'd within a dimension and AND'd across dimensions.

items.question: Will people be notified about tasks?
items.answer: Yes. Creating, updating, completing, and deleting a task publishes a real-time notification. Activities and notes do not trigger notifications.

items.question: How do I edit or remove a task?
items.answer: Open a task in its side sheet to change the description, due date, assignee, links, or completion state. Deleting asks you to confirm and shows the task description first.

activities.title: Activities
activities.description: Calls, meetings, and touchpoints that record real interaction.

blocks.text: Activities record the interactions that actually happened: calls, emails, meetings, notes, and anything else worth logging. Each one carries a type, a subject, a timestamp, and optional detail, and can be tied to a contact or deal. Logged activities are the raw signal behind relationship warmth.

items.title: Pick a type
items.description: Choose Call, Email, Meeting, Note, or Other from the color-coded visual picker. The type shapes how the entry appears on the timeline.

items.title: Add a subject and time
items.description: Give it a subject line and set the moment it happened with a native date and time picker. Add notes for the detail.

items.title: Link it to a record
items.description: Attach the activity to a contact and/or deal so it lands in that record's history.

blocks.title: Activity types
rows: Muted sparkles icon, the fallback for anything unrecognized.

blocks.text: The timeline lists activities newest-first, grouped by date into Today, Yesterday, specific dates, and No date. Each entry shows its type icon, subject, a notes preview, linked contact and deal badges, the creator's avatar, and the time in your locale. Click a badge to jump to that record, or click the entry to edit it. A Week Pulse chart above the timeline plots your activity count for each of the past seven days, highlights today, and totals the week.

items.title: Filter by type
items.description: Show a single type or All, with a count badge per type. Your choice is remembered across sessions.

items.title: Filter by dimension
items.description: Multi-select by creator, contact, deal, or company. Options are drawn from the activities currently in view; selections are OR'd within a dimension and AND'd across them.

items.title: Search
items.description: Full-text, case-insensitive search across subject, notes, linked contact and deal names, and creator name.

items.title: Clear all filters
items.description: Reset search, type, dimensional filters, and grouping to their defaults in one click.

blocks.title: A cover confirms your save
blocks.body: When you create an activity, note, or task, a semi-transparent cover animates over the form with a spinner, then a success checkmark. It blocks interaction until the operation finishes and holds the dialog open briefly so you see the confirmation before it closes.

items.question: Who can see and change activities?
items.answer: Everything is scoped to your current workspace and never crosses to another tenant. Creating, updating, and deleting are governed by role-based permissions, and every change is recorded in the audit trail with the fields that changed.

items.question: What if I enter an unusual activity type?
items.answer: The picker normalizes any input to one of the five known types, matching case-insensitively, and anything unrecognized becomes Other.

items.question: Why do the contact and deal dropdowns scroll on their own?
items.answer: The contact, deal, and user selectors capture the scroll wheel inside the dropdown instead of scrolling the page, so a long list stays contained while you browse it.

items.question: Is Connex usable in Japanese and with a screen reader?
items.answer: Yes. All labels are available in English and Japanese with locale-aware dates and times, controls carry ARIA roles and labels for keyboard and screen-reader use, and animations shorten or skip when you prefer reduced motion.

blocks.text: In Connex, meetings live as activities of the Meeting type, connected to the people and companies they involve. Recording a meeting this way keeps it on the same timeline as your calls, emails, and notes, and lets it count toward relationship warmth like every other interaction.

items.title: Log an activity
items.description: Start a new activity and choose the Meeting type, shown with a violet people icon.

items.title: Set the time
items.description: Use the date and time picker to record when the meeting took place, and add a subject and notes.

items.title: Link the participants
items.description: Attach the meeting to the contact and/or deal involved so it appears in that record's history.

blocks.title: Meetings are signals too
blocks.body: A logged meeting appears in the activity timeline grouped by date and feeds the warmth of the relationships it is linked to, exactly like a call or a note.
