DocsLibrary.title: Library
DocsLibrary.description: Tags, files, saved views, and segments that organize your workspace.
DocsLibrary.lead: The library holds the reusable structure of your workspace: how records are labeled, filed, and sliced.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Flexible labels for grouping and filtering records.

blocks.text: Tags are workspace-scoped labels you apply to contacts, companies, deals, and files to categorize and group related records. The tag library is where you create, edit, delete, and organize every tag in the workspace, each with its own color.

Give each tag a color so it reads at a glance on a record or file. Pick from a curated 16-color palette (slate, red, orange, amber, yellow, lime, green, emerald, teal, cyan, blue, indigo, violet, fuchsia, pink, and rose), or open the native color picker to set any custom hex value.

blocks.title: Copy a hex code
blocks.body: Click a tag's color to copy its hex code to the clipboard, ready to paste into design tools or documentation.

items.title: Search
items.description: Search tags by name or by hex code to jump straight to the one you need.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Sort tags by color in natural spectral order, or alphabetically by name.

blocks.text: You do not have to tag records one at a time. Select multiple records across a contacts, companies, or deals list and add or remove a tag on all of them in a single operation. Files support the same bulk tagging from the Files library.

blocks.title: Starting from empty
blocks.body: A brand-new workspace has no tags. Until you create one, the tag library shows a full-page empty state that walks you through creating your first tag.

files.title: Files
files.description: Attachments stored against records, with previews and detail.

blocks.text: The Files library gathers every file uploaded across the workspace in one place. Each file is linked to a single record (a company, contact, deal, or user), and you can browse, search, filter, tag, and manage all of them from here.

items.title: View modes
items.description: Switch between grid view for visual thumbnails and list view for a tabular layout with details.

items.title: Search
items.description: Search by file name across the entire workspace.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Order files by newest, oldest, name, or file size.

items.title: Pagination
items.description: Files are paginated with a configurable page size from 1 to 100, defaulting to 25 per page.

blocks.text: Narrow the library by file type, by source record type (company, person, deal, or user), by tag, and by orphaned status to show files that are not linked to any record. Facet counts next to each filter show how many files match and update dynamically as you refine.

blocks.title: Deep links carry your view
blocks.body: The library reads filters, search, and the open file from the URL. That means a link can drop someone straight into a specific filtered view, and can even open a particular file's detail sheet on load.

items.title: Detail sheet
items.description: A side panel with the file's type, size, linked record, uploader, upload date, and tag assignments.

items.title: Related files
items.description: See every other file attached to the same record and jump between them from the detail sheet.

items.title: Record link
items.description: Each file belongs to one record; click through to open the owning company, person, deal, or user.

items.title: Image preview
items.description: Image files show a thumbnail on the card and a full-size preview in the detail sheet.

items.title: Open or download
items.description: Open a file in a new tab or download it to your machine directly from the library.

items.title: Tag chips
items.description: Tags appear as colored chips on cards and rows; extra tags beyond the display limit collapse into a '+N' count.

items.title: Bulk actions
items.description: Select multiple files on the page to tag them all at once, or delete them together behind a confirmation dialog.

items.title: Delete
items.description: Remove a single file after confirming its name and size, or clear several at once with bulk delete.

blocks.title: Nothing here yet
blocks.body: When the workspace has no files, an empty state prompts you to upload your first file or create a record to start attaching files to.

saved-views-and-segments.title: Saved views & segments
saved-views-and-segments.description: Reusable, rule-based slices of your records you can return to.

blocks.text: Saved views let you recall a filtered, searched, and sorted record list without rebuilding it each time. They work on companies, contacts, and deals, and each user keeps their own set per record type. Smart segments go further, turning rule-based query logic into a reusable slice you can embed inside a saved view.

items.title: Save a view
items.description: Capture the current filters, search, sort order, and smart segments as a named view for later.

items.title: Update
items.description: Change an existing view's filters, search, sort, or segments and save over it.

items.title: Save as new
items.description: Keep the original untouched and save your modified view under a new name.

items.title: Rename and delete
items.description: Rename a view or remove one you no longer need.

items.title: Tab bar
items.description: Your views appear as clickable tabs for the current record type; the 'All' tab is the default unfiltered list.

blocks.title: The active tab follows your filters
blocks.body: If you adjust filters by hand until they match a saved view, its tab highlights automatically, even though you never clicked it. The tab bar always reflects the view your current filters describe.

blocks.text: A segment is a set of conditions evaluated server-side to return the records that match. It combines graph-aware predicates, which draw on Connex's relationship signals, with plain field comparisons, joined by ALL (every condition must match) or ANY (at least one must match).

blocks.title: Graph-aware predicates (companies)
rows: Companies where you have a warm introduction through a strong connection to someone there.
Companies with at least one open deal.
Companies whose relationship temperature is cool, cold, or trending toward cooling.
Companies with no emails, calls, meetings, or notes in the last N days (default 30, configurable 1 to 3650).

items.title: Field conditions
items.description: Match companies by industry (equals or contains), by name substring, or by a single tag.

items.title: ALL vs ANY
items.description: Join conditions as an intersection (AND) or a union (OR).

items.title: Negate a condition
items.description: Invert any condition, for example 'does NOT have an open deal' or 'is NOT in Fintech'.

items.title: Value options
items.description: Dropdowns auto-populate with the workspace's distinct industries and all its tags.

items.title: Condition chips
items.description: Applied conditions read as chips like 'Has an open deal', with a badge counting the total.

items.title: Clear and reset
items.description: Remove all conditions to return to an unfiltered view.

blocks.title: Evaluated with your permissions
blocks.body: Segments are resolved server-side and return only the records you are allowed to see. Evaluation respects your permissions and record visibility, scoped to the current workspace.

items.question: Are my saved views shared with the workspace?
items.answer: No. Each user keeps their own saved views per record type; yours are not visible to teammates.

items.question: Can a saved view include a segment?
items.answer: Yes. A view captures your filters, search, sort, and any smart segment together, so recalling the view restores the segment too.

DocsData.title: Search, import & data
DocsData.description: Global search, filters, bulk operations, import/export, and custom fields.
DocsData.lead: These tools move data in and out of Connex and help you find and change it at scale.

search.title: Global search
search.description: Search across every record type with keyboard navigation.

blocks.text: Global search reaches across everything in your workspace from one bar. Type at least two characters and Connex looks through users, companies, people, deals, pipelines, tags, activities, notes, tasks, and attachments at once. Input is debounced by 250 milliseconds, so results keep pace with your typing without flooding the backend.

items.title: Every entity type
items.description: One query matches users, companies, people, deals, pipelines, tags, activities, notes, tasks, and attachments.

items.title: Grouped results
items.description: Matches are grouped by entity type in a fixed order, so people always sit with people and deals with deals.

items.title: Readable metadata
items.description: Each result shows a leading avatar, icon, or coloured tag dot, a label, and a subtitle such as an email, title, industry, website, deal value, or file size.

items.title: Two surfaces
items.description: Results appear in the dropdown under the search bar, or on a dedicated search page with group headings and per-group counts.

items.action: Focus the search input from anywhere on the page
Move the selection up and down the result list
Open the selected result, or the full search page if nothing is selected

blocks.title: The dropdown opens even when empty
blocks.body: Clicking the search bar or pressing '/' opens the dropdown right away. If your query already has two or more characters, results appear immediately; otherwise you see a placeholder until you type enough to match.

items.question: Why do results seem to have a fixed order?
items.answer: Groups are shown in a set sequence (users, companies, people, deals, pipelines, tags, activities, notes, tasks, attachments). Within a group, results appear in the order the backend returns them.

items.question: Why is my query not returning anything?
items.answer: Search needs a minimum of two characters. A single character shows the placeholder rather than running a query.

items.question: Why are some labels cut off?
items.answer: Labels and subtitles truncate at around 70 characters so the dropdown stays readable. Open the result or the full search page to see the complete record.

filters-and-bulk.title: Filters & bulk actions
filters-and-bulk.description: Narrow a table, select many rows, and act on them at once.

blocks.text: Record lists for contacts, companies, and deals share a common toolbar: dropdown filters to narrow the list, and bulk actions to change many records at once. Filters and bulk actions work together, so you can filter down to exactly the set you want and then act on all of it in a single request.

items.title: Multi-select filters
items.description: Pick several values at once from checklists such as companies, titles, or tags. Each option shows a live count of matching records.

items.title: Radio filters
items.description: Single-choice controls set things like sort order or view mode.

items.title: Contact facets
items.description: The contacts list adds a company multi-select, a title multi-select, and a 'no company' toggle. Companies and titles come from the backend as facets.

items.title: Active filter pills
items.description: Applied filters show as pills with counts. Clear one pill at a time or reset them all at once.

blocks.title: Pills tell you what is active at a glance
blocks.body: A filter pill with a selection takes on a brand-coloured background and a count badge, while inactive pills stay muted. That colour shift is the fastest way to see which filters are narrowing your list.

blocks.title: Act on many records at once

items.title: Tag add and remove
items.description: Select records with the checkboxes, then add or remove a tag across all of them in one request.

items.title: Delete records
items.description: Delete every selected record in a single request.

items.title: Assign deal owner
items.description: Reassign selected deals to a new owner, or unassign them. The owner must be a workspace member.

items.title: Change deal stage
items.description: Move selected deals to a new stage, which must exist in the workspace pipelines.

blocks.title: One failure does not stop the rest
blocks.body: Bulk operations run per record. The response returns a succeeded count, a failed count, and a per-row list of reasons, so a single record that cannot be found or updated never blocks the others. Duplicate IDs in a request are de-duplicated and processed once.

blocks.title: Very large selections are chunked automatically
blocks.body: A bulk request over 1000 records is split client-side into sequential batches of 1000. The batches are merged back into one combined result, with row indexes offset so you still see a single outcome.

import-and-export.title: Import & export
import-and-export.description: Bring records in from CSV and take your data back out.

blocks.text: Import brings records into Connex from a CSV file through a guided wizard, and export sends them back out as a clean, spreadsheet-ready CSV. Import parses your file in the browser, then validates and writes on the backend, so you always see what will happen before anything is created or changed.

items.title: Upload
items.description: Choose a CSV file. It is parsed in the browser and checked against the file limits before anything is sent.

items.title: Map
items.description: Match each CSV column to a Connex field, choose to create a custom field, or leave a column unmapped to ignore it.

items.title: Review
items.description: A dry-run preview shows each row's outcome, deduplication matches, and any errors, with no writes yet.

items.title: Done
items.description: Commit the import to create and update records in bulk, then review the created, updated, and skipped counts.

items.title: Standard or custom fields
items.description: Map a column to a Connex field, or pick 'Create custom field' to auto-create a new definition on first import. See the custom fields guide for detail.

items.title: Tags column
items.description: A column named 'tags' can hold comma or semicolon-separated names. Missing tags are created and attached, defaulting to a neutral colour.

items.title: Contact company linking
items.description: A 'company' column on contact imports auto-creates companies if missing, links them, and records employment history.

items.title: Deal people linking
items.description: A 'people' column on deal imports holds comma or semicolon-separated emails. Matching contacts are linked; unknown emails are skipped quietly.

items.title: Deal pipeline and stage
items.description: Deals reference pipelines and stages by name, resolved case-insensitively. Missing values fall back to the first pipeline and its first stage.

blocks.title: Validation and normalisation on import
rows: Required on contacts, companies, and deals. Trimmed. Must not exceed 255 characters.
Must match a standard address pattern. Normalised to lowercase and trimmed.
Normalised to lowercase with http://, www., and trailing slashes stripped.
Must parse as a valid YYYY-MM-DD date.
Must parse as a number; custom number fields expect a parseable value.
Accepts an http:// prefix or a plain domain pattern.
Defaults to USD when a row has no currency value.
Landing a deal in a won or lost stage sets its won flag and auto-fills closedAt and closedReason if unset.

items.title: Match keys
items.description: Rows are matched against existing records on high-confidence keys: contact email, company website or name, and deal name plus company.

items.title: Three merge strategies
items.description: Choose 'fill empty' to populate only null fields, 'skip' to ignore matching rows, or 'overwrite' to replace all fields. Each row's outcome is previewed before commit.

items.title: Manual row linking
items.description: In review, link a row to a specific existing record through a search overlay, overriding automatic dedup. Linked rows show a badge and can be unlinked.

items.title: In-file deduplication
items.description: If several rows produce the same key within one file, later duplicates are marked 'skip' rather than creating multiple records.

blocks.title: Fix failed rows and re-import
body: When rows fail, the done step offers a 'Download errors' button. It produces a CSV with your original columns plus an 'error' column, containing only the failed rows with their reason, so you can correct the data and import again.
The frontend also rejects files over 5 MB or with more than 5000 data rows before they reach the backend.

items.title: Filter parity
items.description: Export honours the same filters as the list view: contacts respect the search query, company, title, and 'no company' filters; companies respect tags or specific ids; deals respect pipeline, stage, company, contact, and tag filters.

items.title: Full column structure
items.description: Exports include standard columns, then one column per active custom-field definition sorted by position, then a 'tags' column with comma-separated tag names.

items.title: Spreadsheet-safe encoding
items.description: Files are RFC-4180 CSV with a UTF-8 byte order mark, so Excel and Sheets detect the encoding and render non-ASCII characters correctly.

items.title: Formula injection protection
items.description: Cells beginning with =, +, -, @, tab, or carriage return are prefixed with an apostrophe on export and unescaped on import, guarding against spreadsheet formula injection.

items.title: Audited operations
items.description: Every import commit writes a single audit entry (not one per row) with its created, updated, and skipped counts. Exports and searches are logged too, keeping the trail readable yet complete.

custom-fields.title: Custom fields
custom-fields.description: Extend records with fields specific to your workspace.

blocks.text: Custom fields let you store data Connex does not model out of the box, such as a customer number, a renewal date, or a preference flag. They belong to an entity type, carry a typed value, and show up on record detail pages and in exports alongside the standard fields.

The most common way to add a custom field is straight from the import wizard. When a CSV column has no matching Connex field, choose 'Create custom field' in the mapping step, pick a type, and the backend persists a new definition the first time the import runs. The wizard infers a likely type client-side by sampling the first 50 non-empty cells in the column.

blocks.title: How a custom field is defined

items.title: Entity type
items.description: Each definition belongs to one entity type, so a field on contacts is separate from one on companies or deals.

items.title: Field key and label
items.description: The label you enter becomes the human-readable name; its slug becomes the stable field key used under the hood.

items.title: Field type
items.description: Pick from text, number, date, boolean, or url. The type governs how values are validated and displayed.

items.title: Where it appears
items.description: Once created, the definition surfaces on record detail pages and as its own column in exports.

blocks.title: Value validation by type
rows: A value that parses as a number (double).
An http:// prefix or a plain domain pattern.

blocks.title: Definitions persist and export
blocks.body: A custom field created during import is stored as a reusable definition, not a one-off value. It then appears on every matching record's detail page and gets its own column in future exports, sorted by its position among the non-archived definitions.

items.title: Import & export
items.description: Map columns, create fields on the fly, and see how custom fields flow into exported CSVs.

DocsCollaboration.title: Collaboration
DocsCollaboration.description: Invites, invite links, record sharing, permissions, notifications, and mentions.
DocsCollaboration.lead: Connex is multiplayer. These pages cover how you bring people in and work together without crossing tenant lines.

invites-and-links.title: Invites & invite links
invites-and-links.description: Add teammates directly or with a shareable link.

text: There are two ways to bring people into a workspace, and both are handled by admins and owners. You can invite a specific person by email, or you can create a reusable link and share it with a group. Either way, the new person always confirms before they gain access.
Every workspace member you add joins as a role you choose, and nothing they do can cross into another tenant.

items.title: Existing Connex users
items.description: If the email already belongs to a Connex account, the person is added as a pending member and notified in the app. They still have to accept before they join.

items.title: Brand-new emails
items.description: If the email is not yet on Connex, a token-based invite link is generated that you can share so they can sign up and join.

items.title: Add someone directly
items.description: You can search for an existing Connex user and add them without composing an invite. They arrive as a pending member and get the same in-app notification.

items.title: One invite per email
items.description: An email address can hold only one pending invite at a time. Sending a new one supersedes the earlier invite.

items.title: Open the invitation
items.description: Existing users find it under Workspace Invitations in Settings, or by following the invite link. The link opens a preview page.

items.title: Review the details
items.description: The preview shows the workspace name, the role being granted, and who invited you when that is available. Invalid or expired invites show a friendly error instead.

items.title: Accept or decline
items.description: Accepting joins you to the workspace as the assigned role. Declining removes the invitation and its notification.

blocks.title: An invite is addressed to one email
blocks.body: Token invites are bound to the exact address they were sent to. If you are signed in with a different email, Connex blocks the acceptance and tells you the invite went to another address. Emails are normalized to lowercase and trimmed, and each one is validated before it is used.

blocks.text: A shareable link is not tied to a single email. Any authenticated user can redeem it to join, up to an optional cap, until it expires or you revoke it. Redeeming the same link twice never creates a duplicate membership, so a link is safe to circulate.

blocks.title: Link settings
rows: Member or admin. Defaults to member and is fixed once the link is created.
Days until the link stops working. Defaults to 14 days when left empty.
How many people can redeem it. Empty means unlimited.
Restricts which email domains may join through the link. Empty means unrestricted.

blocks.title: The allowlist only guards links
blocks.body: A domain allowlist applies to self-serve link joins, never to explicit email invites, which are always allowed. Domains are normalized to lowercase and a leading @ is stripped. Formats that are missing a dot, contain spaces, or have multiple @ signs are rejected with a helpful message. Anyone whose domain is not on the list is turned away when they try to redeem.

items.question: Where do I see what is outstanding?
items.answer: Settings > Members shows two lists: Pending Invites (email invites not yet accepted) and Active Links (shareable links still valid). Each shows the role and expiry, and links also show the used count against the max cap.

items.question: How do I copy an invite or link?
items.answer: From Pending Invites you can copy the accept link for any invite. From Active Links a dedicated button copies the link URL and shows a checkmark for a moment as confirmation.

items.question: Can I cancel an invite?
items.answer: Yes. Admins can revoke a pending email invite, which removes it from the list and prevents it from being accepted.

items.question: How do I shut off a shareable link?
items.answer: Revoke it. The link is marked revoked, drops off the Active Links list, and stops accepting any further redemptions.

sharing-and-permissions.title: Sharing & permissions
sharing-and-permissions.description: Share individual records and control who can see what.

text: Two separate mechanisms control who can do what. Roles govern what a member can do inside their own workspace, and record sharing exposes an individual record to another workspace you also belong to.
Both are managed by admins and owners, and every change is written to the audit log.

items.title: Owner
items.description: Full control, including managing members, roles, and sharing, plus reassigning ownership and deleting the workspace.

items.title: Admin
items.description: Can manage members, invites, and shares, but cannot delete the workspace.

items.title: Member
items.description: Reads and writes records with no admin powers.

blocks.text: Owners can go beyond the built-in roles. The permission catalog lists every permission, such as COMPANY_CREATE or COMPANY_UPDATE, grouped by entity type like Company, Person, Deal, Task, Share, and Role, and shows which permissions each built-in role grants. An owner can create a custom role by selecting any subset of those permissions, toggling them individually or a whole group at once, then assign it to members in place of a built-in role. Custom roles can be edited or deleted, and Connex makes sure no member is left pointing at a role that no longer exists, so a role in use is reassigned before it can be removed.

items.title: See everyone
items.description: Every active member appears with their name, email, role, and profile picture. You are marked You, and pending members carry a Pending badge.

items.title: Change roles
items.description: Admins promote or demote between member and admin and assign custom roles, and owners can reassign ownership. Membership must be active to change a role, so a pending member can only be removed, not re-roled.

items.title: Remove members
items.description: Admins can remove any active member except themselves, and removal takes effect immediately. A workspace cannot lose its only owner, so ownership must be transferred first.

blocks.text: An admin can share a record from one workspace with another workspace the same person belongs to. Sharing is available for companies, contacts, and pipelines only. The owning workspace keeps full ownership, and the receiving workspace gains read visibility, plus edit access if you grant it.

blocks.title: Sharing rules
rows: Shared records are read-only for the recipient. Toggle can-edit on to grant edit access as well.
Records can be shared only with workspaces in the same organization. Cross-organization attempts are rejected with a clear message.
A record cannot be shared with its own workspace.
Admins can view every workspace a record is shared with, along with the shared date and edit status, and unshare at any time. Unsharing removes the record from the recipient immediately.

blocks.title: Everything is audited
blocks.body: Invites created, revoked, and accepted, links created and revoked, shares granted and revoked, and members added, removed, or role-changed are all recorded in the audit log with the actor, the action, and a description.

notifications-and-mentions.title: Notifications & mentions
notifications-and-mentions.description: Stay in the loop with an inbox and @-mentions on records.

text: Connex watches your data and raises notifications so you do not have to. Tasks that are due, deals that are closing, relationships that are cooling, and people worth introducing all surface on their own.

Every notification from every workspace you belong to lands in one unified inbox. Recipients are identified globally, so switching workspaces never changes what you see. Mentioning a teammate on a record notifies them here too.

items.title: Task due reminders
items.description: Fire when a task is due soon, about seven days ahead by default, and again once it is overdue. Approaching tasks are warnings, overdue tasks are critical, and you can tick the task complete straight from the notification.

items.title: Deal close-date reminders
items.description: Warn as a deal's expected close date approaches and turn critical once it passes. The deal owner and every collaborator on the deal team are notified.

items.title: Relationship cooling nudges
items.description: Trigger after roughly two weeks without contact. Severity follows the relationship's temperature band, and each nudge offers a Log touch button to warm the relationship back up.

items.title: Introduction opportunities
items.description: Surface the top few pairs of people worth connecting, shared with every workspace member as informational notices.

blocks.title: Why a nudge is marked Priority
rows: A related deal is expected to close within 14 days.
The deal sits in the top quarter by value. This needs at least four open deals to rank meaningfully, otherwise the signal is off.
The deal is at least 75 percent of the way through its pipeline.
The contact's role contains champion, decision, buyer, or sponsor.

text: The bell in the top navigation shows your unread count, capping the badge at 99+ once you pass 99, and refreshes every 45 seconds or whenever the tab returns to the foreground. Clicking it opens a compact dropdown with up to eight of your most recent unread notifications, each body clamped to two lines.

The full inbox page shows 20 notifications per page with page controls, full untruncated bodies, relative times like 5 minutes ago, and a color-coded icon per type. Unread notifications carry a bold title and a colored dot; read ones gray out but stay in the Active view. Notifications from other workspaces show a small tag naming their source, empty views tell you that you are all caught up, and content shimmers in with placeholder cards while it loads.

items.title: Read and unread
items.description: Toggle any notification between read and unread, or clear the whole list with Mark all read from either the bell or the inbox.

items.title: Dismiss and restore
items.description: Dismiss a notification to move it to History, then restore it back to Active from there if you need it again.

items.title: Snooze
items.description: Hide an active notification for 1 day, 3 days, or 1 week. It reappears on the next refresh if the underlying condition still holds.

items.title: Quick actions
items.description: Complete a task, log a touch, or open the related record inline. The same alerts also appear as banners on the matching contact, deal, or task page, and each carries the context it needs to act without a second load.

blocks.title: Inbox views
rows: Unread and read notifications that are not dismissed or resolved.
Notifications you dismissed and ones Connex auto-resolved.

blocks.title: Nudges will not nag you
body: Once a cooling nudge exists it stays until the relationship genuinely warms up or you touch the contact, so a transient dip in the trend does not make the same nudge flicker back at you.
Clicking a notification to open its record also marks it read, even if it was unread, so acting on something clears it for you.

items.question: How does Connex keep the inbox current?
items.answer: A background service reconciles expected against actual notifications. When a task, deal, or relationship changes, a partial pass for that workspace runs right after the change commits, off the main thread. Every five minutes a full pass also rescores relationship decay and recomputes introduction opportunities, which is the only pass that surfaces new relationship nudges and intros. A dedupe key per notification means these passes can safely re-run without creating duplicates, and anything whose condition no longer applies is auto-resolved.

items.question: Can I turn off types I do not want?
items.answer: Yes. A settings page lets you independently enable or disable task reminders, deal reminders, and relationship cooling nudges. A wildcard default covers any type you have not set explicitly, and a specific preference always takes precedence over it.

items.question: Why did my old overdue items not appear?
items.answer: On first run Connex avoids flooding your inbox. Overdue tasks and deals are only backfilled if they became overdue within the last 30 days, and a cooling nudge is not created for a contact that has already been cold for more than 90 days. Existing nudges keep evolving normally, and old reminders are purged after 90 days.

items.question: Are due dates in my time zone?
items.answer: Yes. Task and deal reminders compute due and close dates in your local time zone, not UTC, so a task due on the 24th is judged against your local date.

items.question: What happens when someone mentions me?
items.answer: Mentioning a teammate on a record notifies them in this same inbox, alongside your other notifications. The person you mention must be a member of the workspace.

items.question: Is the inbox accessible?
items.answer: Yes. Interactive elements carry screen-reader labels, and the bell button announces the unread count.

DocsSettings.title: Settings & administration
DocsSettings.description: Members, roles and RBAC, rules and automation, notification settings, and audit logs.
DocsSettings.lead: Administration controls who can do what, automates routine work, and keeps a record of every change.

members-and-roles.title: Members & roles
members-and-roles.description: Manage who is in the workspace and what their role permits.

text: Membership and roles decide who can enter your workspace and what they can do once inside. Every workspace is tenant-isolated, so people only ever see the workspace they belong to, and their role governs each action they take.

Members with the admin role or higher manage other people. Owners sit above admins and can promote an admin all the way to owner. These settings live in the workspace settings area, alongside rules, custom fields, and notifications.

items.title: What you see
items.description: Each member row shows their name, email, avatar, and current role, with a pending badge if they have not accepted yet.

items.title: Change a role
items.description: Open the row menu and pick a new role inline. Admins can assign member or admin; owners can also assign any custom role.

items.title: Remove a member
items.description: Removing someone asks for confirmation first. The change applies immediately and reverts if it fails.

items.title: Your own row
items.description: Your row carries a You badge and its action menu is disabled, so you cannot change or remove yourself.

items.title: Owner
items.description: Full control. Only owners create and edit custom roles and assign system-mode automation rules.

items.title: Admin
items.description: Manages members, invites, custom fields, and most workspace settings, but cannot touch owner-only areas.

items.title: Member
items.description: The default role. Works with records according to the permissions granted to it.

items.title: Custom roles
items.description: Owners build roles from a permission catalog grouped by entity (company, person, deal, and more), each with humanized create, update, and delete actions.

blocks.title: Owners hold the keys
blocks.body: The three built-in roles are fixed and cannot be edited. Only owners can create or edit custom roles and assign system-mode rules. When someone without permission opens one of these sections, they see a centered No access message or a 403 page instead of the settings.

items.title: Email invite
items.description: Invite by email address. If the address already belongs to a Connex user they join as pending with an in-app notification; otherwise they get an invite link that expires in 14 days by default.

items.title: Shareable invite link
items.description: Create a reusable link with an optional expiry in days and a maximum use count. It is copied to your clipboard on creation, shows its usage, and can be revoked at any time.

items.title: Email domain auto-join
items.description: Whitelist a domain so anyone who signs up with that email domain joins automatically with the default member role.

items.title: Accepting and leaving
items.description: Invitees accept or decline pending workspaces from the Membership tab, and can leave a workspace there, with a warning if it is their only one.

blocks.title: Custom field types
rows: A date chosen from a picker.

items.question: Can I change a field's type or key later?
items.answer: No. A field's type and its machine key are permanent once created. The key is derived from the label by slugifying it (lowercase, up to 64 characters), with a hashed fallback if the label is empty, and it never changes so stored data stays intact.

items.question: How do select fields work?
items.answer: You define at least one option label. Each option stores a unique auto-generated key while showing your label in the dropdown, and you can add or remove options while editing the field.

items.question: What happens when I lack permission for a section?
items.answer: You see a centered No access message instead of the interface, and owner-only areas return a 403 page.

items.question: Why did a change I made snap back?
items.answer: Settings update optimistically: the change shows at once, then syncs. If the backend rejects it, the change reverts and an error toast appears. While a section is still loading, skeleton placeholders show its layout.

items.question: Where are the edit and delete actions?
items.answer: Every row has a three-dot menu that appears on hover or focus, consistent across members, roles, fields, and rules. Destructive actions always ask for confirmation first, and empty sections show a short message describing what will appear once you add something.

rules-and-automation.title: Rules & automation
rules-and-automation.description: Automate routine changes with workspace rules.

text: Rules automate routine work. When a record changes, or on a repeating schedule, a rule runs a list of actions so you do not have to. Rules are created by members with permission to manage them and can be turned on or off at any time.
Each rule runs off-thread after the triggering change is committed, so automation never slows down the action that set it off.

items.title: A trigger
items.description: What starts the rule: a record change, or a schedule.

items.title: An optional condition
items.description: A WHEN clause that narrows which records the rule applies to. Available for company rules.

items.title: A list of actions
items.description: The THEN steps the rule performs when it fires.

items.title: A run-as mode
items.description: Whether the rule acts as you or as the workspace itself.

blocks.title: Trigger events by record type
rows: Created, stage changed, won, lost, or updated.

blocks.title: Schedules are for companies
blocks.body: A rule can also run on a repeating schedule (hourly, daily, or weekly), but only for companies, and only with a condition that selects which companies to process. Conditions use a segment builder with all/any logic, predicates like warm intro available, open deal, cooling, or no activity, and field comparisons on industry, name, or tag. Leaving the event list empty on a change trigger means any event, and scheduled runs are bucketed per cadence so a rule cannot fire twice in the same window.

blocks.title: What a rule can do
rows: Sends an in-app notification with a title and body.
Creates a task with a title and a due date, three days out by default.
Logs an activity with a type and subject.

items.title: Run as you
items.description: USER mode acts as the rule's run-as member and is bound by that person's permissions.

items.title: Run as the workspace
items.description: SYSTEM mode acts as a global system actor with a fixed, narrow permission set. Only admins can create system rules, useful for workspace-wide automation the creator could not perform alone.

items.title: Enable or disable
items.description: A switch on each rule turns it on or off. A disabled rule keeps its configuration but never runs, and the toggle updates instantly.

items.title: Execution history
items.description: Each rule keeps a log of its last 50 runs with the time, outcome, and any errors, visible in the rule's detail view.

items.question: What does a rule require to be valid?
items.answer: A name is always required. Change triggers need at least one event, schedule triggers need a condition, notify and create-task actions need a title, log-activity needs an activity type, and add-tag needs a tag selected.

items.question: What due date do created tasks get?
items.answer: Three days out by default. You can set any number of days from one upward.

items.question: Can I pick more than one trigger event?
items.answer: Yes. Select any combination of events for a change trigger. An empty selection behaves as any event.

notification-settings.title: Notification settings
notification-settings.description: Tune which events reach you and how.

text: Notifications keep you on top of what needs attention without hunting for it. The inbox surfaces tasks coming due, deals won or closed, and relationships that are cooling, each scoped to you and carrying the context that produced it.
A bell in the header shows your unread count and updates in real time.

items.title: Unread badge
items.description: The bell shows your unread count and refreshes live, with separate tallies for active, dismissed, and archived notifications.

items.title: Filter and page
items.description: Page through your inbox (25 at a time) and filter by state, category, or the record a notification relates to.

items.title: Jump to the source
items.description: Each notification carries its context (a deal, company, person, or task). Clicking one takes you straight to that record.

items.title: Mark all as read
items.description: Clear your unread count in one action across every active notification.

items.title: Read or unread
items.description: Mark a single notification read or unread to track what you have handled.

items.title: Dismiss
items.description: Archive a notification to move it out of your active list.

items.title: Restore
items.description: Bring a dismissed notification back if you archived it too soon.

items.title: Snooze
items.description: Temporarily hide a notification and let it return later.

blocks.title: Snoozed notifications come back
blocks.body: Snoozing hides a notification for 1, 4, 8, or 24 hours. When the interval passes it reappears in your inbox, so a snooze defers a reminder rather than dismissing it.

blocks.title: Notification types
rows: A task you own is due today or overdue.
A deal is won or lost.
A company or person relationship is cooling or at risk.

blocks.title: Preferences and the wildcard default
blocks.body: You can switch each notification type on or off for the in-app channel. If a specific type has no explicit setting, it falls back to the wildcard preference, and everything defaults to enabled, so you receive notifications until you opt out.

audit-logs.title: Audit logs
audit-logs.description: A tamper-evident history of actions taken in the workspace.

text: The audit log is a complete, append-only history of everything that happens in your workspace. You will find it at Admin, then Logs, as a timeline grouped by day with the newest events first.

Connex records events automatically as people work, so nothing depends on anyone remembering to log it. The log is workspace-scoped, so you only ever see events from the workspace you are in, and it is tamper-evident: the database blocks any attempt to edit or delete a recorded event.

blocks.title: Admins and owners only
blocks.body: Viewing the audit log requires the audit-read permission, which is granted to workspace admins and owners. Members and other roles cannot open it.

items.title: Who
items.description: The actor's name is snapshotted at the time of the action, so a later rename does not rewrite history, while the current name is also shown. System automation appears as System.

items.title: What
items.description: One of more than sixty action types across every entity, shown as friendly labels like created, updated, added tag, or logged in.

items.title: On what
items.description: The target entity and its label at the time, preserved even if the record is later renamed or deleted.

items.title: Outcome
items.description: Success or failure, so operations that hit an error are easy to surface.

items.title: Request context
items.description: The client IP (read from X-Forwarded-For where present), the User-Agent, and a request ID shared by every event from the same request.

blocks.title: Recorded automatically, and never in the way
blocks.body: A single audit service records entity changes, tag operations, sharing, role changes, authentication, CSV imports, and even searches. It is designed never to throw, so a logging failure can never interrupt the action being audited, and the log table is append-only at the database level.

items.title: Search
items.description: Find events by actor, target, action, or summary. Search runs over the loaded events and ignores punctuation.

items.title: Filter
items.description: Narrow by action, entity type, outcome (success or failed), date range (all time, today, last 7 or 30 days), and actor, including the system actor.

items.title: Chips and counts
items.description: Active filters appear as removable chips, and each filter option shows how many events match it so you can predict the result.

items.title: Sort
items.description: Flip between newest-first and oldest-first, which reorders both the day groups and the events within them.

items.title: Field changes
items.description: Each changed field with its old value in red and new value in green. Cleared fields read as empty in italics, and non-text values are shown as JSON.

items.title: Errors
items.description: For a failed event, the error message appears in a red box above any changes.

items.title: Request metadata
items.description: The IP address, User-Agent, and request ID behind the event.

items.title: Related events
items.description: Events from the same request share a request ID, so one action that changed several things can be traced together. If nothing changed, the row says so explicitly.

blocks.title: Reading the log at a glance

items.question: How is the timeline organized?
items.answer: Events are grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, or a dated header with the weekday), each showing a count, and a result line tells you how many events match your filters out of those loaded.

items.question: What are the chart and stats at the top?
items.answer: A 14-day pulse bar chart shows event volume per day with today highlighted, and a stats cluster shows total events, failed events, unique actors, and when the last event happened.

items.question: How do I spot problems quickly?
items.answer: Event icons are color-coded by type (green create, blue update, red delete, violet auth, gray view, amber other), and failed events carry a red Failed badge. The outcome filter isolates failures.

items.question: Why do the timestamps keep changing?
items.answer: Times are shown relative (for example, 3 minutes ago) and refresh about every minute. Hover any timestamp to see the exact date and time.

items.question: Can I see the history of a single record?
items.answer: Yes. Alongside the workspace-wide recent feed, each record has its own change history.

items.question: What do the empty states mean?
items.answer: A workspace with no events shows No activity recorded. If your filters match nothing, a No matching events message offers a Clear all button to restore the full list.

items.question: Are there limits on what is stored?
items.answer: Long values are truncated to sensible limits (for example, User-Agent to 512 characters) to keep the log lean, and a single query returns between 1 and 200 events.

items.question: Does it work from the keyboard?
items.answer: Yes. Rows are focusable buttons that expand with Space or Enter, all filters are keyboard-operable, and rows animate smoothly unless you prefer reduced motion.

DocsPreferences.title: Preferences & the little things
DocsPreferences.description: Theming, language, keyboard shortcuts, and the small quirks worth knowing.
DocsPreferences.lead: The details. How Connex looks, speaks your language, responds to the keyboard, and the tiny behaviors that make it feel considered.

theming-and-appearance.title: Theming & appearance
theming-and-appearance.description: Light, dark, and system themes across the whole app.

text: Connex ships with a light theme, a dark theme, and a system option that follows your operating system. Your choice applies to the whole app, from records and charts to dialogs and menus, and it takes effect instantly without a page reload.

The look is driven by design tokens rather than one-off colors. More than 150 CSS variables (background, foreground, cards, borders, brand color, warmth tokens, and chart colors) swap together when the theme changes, so every surface stays consistent.

items.title: Open the theme menu
items.description: It lives in the sidebar footer, alongside your account controls.

items.title: Pick Light, Dark, or System
items.description: A check mark shows the active choice. System tracks your OS setting automatically.

items.title: See it apply at once
items.description: The theme switches immediately, with no reload, and is remembered for next time.

blocks.title: Everything adapts together
blocks.body: Switching the theme re-derives every token at once. Brand green, warmth badges, and chart colors are all recalculated for the active mode, so contrast stays readable in both light and dark.

items.title: Brand color
items.description: Connex green anchors buttons, active states, highlights, and focus rings, with lighter and darker variants for hover and depth. Dark mode retunes it for legibility.

items.title: Typography
items.description: Inter carries body text, Instrument Serif handles display headings, and Noto Sans JP renders Japanese, with a fallback order that keeps every script sharp.

items.title: Warmth badges
items.description: Relationship temperature uses a fixed palette: hot, warm, cool, and cold each get their own color and dot indicator so a list scans at a glance.

items.title: Chart colors
items.description: A dedicated set of chart tokens keeps data visualizations consistent, with distinct colors for won, lost, and open deals. They follow the theme too.

items.title: Inputs
items.description: Fields share one style: a muted background, a focus ring in brand green, and a red ring for invalid states, so forms feel uniform everywhere.

items.title: Rounded corners
items.description: A single base radius scales into a family of sizes, giving cards, buttons, and dialogs a consistent, softly rounded shape.

items.title: Dialogs and sheets
items.description: Modal dialogs open centered while sheets slide in from the side. Both zoom and fade in, then reverse on close, over a lightly blurred backdrop.

items.title: Motion preferences
items.description: Every animation respects the reduced-motion setting. If you prefer less movement, dialog, sidebar, chart, and node animations are skipped.

items.title: Backdrop blur
items.description: Overlays dim the page and apply a subtle blur, with a graceful fallback where the browser does not support the effect.

items.title: Close control
items.description: Every modal carries a labeled close button in the top-right corner, so a dialog is always one click, or one Escape press, away from dismissal.

blocks.title: Form dialogs cascade in
blocks.body: Open a form dialog and its parts do not all appear at once. The header, fields, buttons, and footer rise in with a short staggered delay, creating a gentle cascade. Turn on reduced motion and the cascade disappears.

language-and-i18n.title: Language & internationalization
language-and-i18n.description: Switch between English and Japanese anywhere.

text: Connex is fully bilingual in English and Japanese. Every part of the interface is translated, spread across eighteen message files that cover common UI, authentication, the dashboard, records, and more, so switching language changes the whole app rather than a handful of labels.
You can change the language from the landing pages or from within the app, and your choice carries across sessions.

items.title: Open the language switcher
items.description: Look for the globe icon. It shows the current language and lists English and Japanese.

items.title: Choose a language
items.description: A check mark marks the active language. The interface briefly dims while it refreshes into the new locale.

items.title: Carry on
items.description: The whole app re-renders in your chosen language, including dates, labels, and messages.

blocks.title: Your choice is remembered
blocks.body: The selected language is stored in a cookie, so it survives page refreshes and returning after you close the browser. If no choice is stored, Connex falls back to English.

blocks.text: Japanese is not just translated text. When content is Japanese, Connex renders it in Noto Sans JP, a typeface designed for the script, while Latin text continues to use Inter. The fallback order keeps both readable even when a screen mixes languages.

blocks.title: Fonts follow the language
blocks.body: You never pick a font by hand. The type family switches automatically with the locale, so choosing Japanese also brings in the right Japanese typeface without any extra step.

items.title: Theming and appearance
items.description: How themes, colors, and typography come together across the app.

blocks.text: Connex is built to be driven from the keyboard. Global search, menus, comboboxes, and dialogs all respond to keys, so you can move through the app without reaching for the mouse.

items.action: Move through search results or a menu
Open the highlighted result or confirm a choice
Dismiss the open search, menu, or dialog

blocks.text: The search bar is a command palette over your whole workspace. It searches across more than eleven entity types, including companies, contacts, deals, pipelines, tags, activities, notes, tasks, files, and users. Input is debounced so results keep pace with your typing, and results are grouped by type with an icon or color dot for quick scanning.

items.title: Keyboard navigation
items.description: Arrow up and down cycle through results, Enter opens the highlighted one, and Escape closes the palette.

items.title: Auto-scroll
items.description: As you arrow past the visible area, the highlighted result scrolls itself into view so it never slips off screen.

items.title: Type cues
items.description: Companies and contacts show avatars, other types show a category icon, and tags show a color dot, so you can tell results apart at a glance.

items.title: Tidy snippets
items.description: Long note and task text is truncated with an ellipsis, keeping each result on a single readable line.

blocks.title: Two characters to start
blocks.body: Search waits until you have typed at least two characters before showing results, which keeps a single keystroke from flooding the palette. From there, arrowing past the bottom of the list quietly scrolls the highlight back into view.

items.title: Dropdown menus
items.description: Arrow keys move through items, Enter or Space activates, and Escape closes. Submenus and click-outside dismissal work as you would expect.

items.title: Comboboxes and autocomplete
items.description: Searchable selects support single and multi-select, chips, grouped options, and a clear button, with the highlighted option scrolling into view.

items.title: Instant tooltips
items.description: Tooltips appear the moment you hover, with no delay, and point to their trigger from whichever side fits the viewport.

items.title: Visible focus
items.description: Keyboard focus always shows a clear ring in brand green on buttons, inputs, links, and menu items, so you can see where you are.

blocks.title: Built for assistive tech
blocks.body: Interactive elements carry proper ARIA roles and labels, and the layout uses semantic HTML throughout, so screen readers can follow along. Dropdowns open on click, and on the keyboard via Enter or Space, matching standard menu behavior.

tips-and-quirks.title: Tips & quirks
tips-and-quirks.description: Small behaviors and details that reward knowing.

blocks.text: Beyond the big features, Connex is full of small behaviors that make it feel considered. This page collects the details worth knowing: profile touches, notification timing, layout rules, and a few scrolling quirks.

items.title: Inline profile editing
items.description: The pencil icon opens a modal to change your username, display name, email, and picture, with field-level validation as you go.

items.title: Instant picture preview
items.description: Drop in a new profile picture and you see a rounded preview immediately, with no server round-trip, cleared again if you close without saving.

items.title: Workspace switcher
items.description: Switch between workspaces or create a new one from a dropdown that shows your current tenant and how many you belong to.

items.title: Workspace glyph
items.description: Each workspace is marked by a glyph, the first letter of its name in a brand-green square, so you can recognize it without a logo.

blocks.title: Small touches
body: Your profile page greets you with one of nine rotating greetings, so it rarely opens the same way twice.
Save the profile form without actually changing anything and Connex notices: instead of a pointless request, it simply tells you there is nothing to save.

items.title: Unread badge
items.description: The bell shows your unread count, refreshing about every 45 seconds and again the moment you refocus the tab. It pauses while the tab is hidden.

items.title: Counts across workspaces
items.description: The unread count is scoped to you, not a single tenant, so it reflects everything unread across every workspace you belong to.

items.title: Toasts
items.description: Brief messages appear top-center for success, error, warning, and info, themed to match light or dark mode, and dismiss on their own or on demand.

items.title: Form feedback
items.description: Field errors appear beneath the input in red, loading buttons show a spinner and lock to prevent double-submits, and empty screens offer a clear next step.

items.title: Sidebar toggle
items.description: Hide or show the sidebar on desktop, and its state persists. On mobile it becomes an overlay that closes on route change or Escape.

items.title: Collapsible sections
items.description: The sidebar groups navigation into sections you can fold away, with an arrow that rotates to show open or closed state.

items.title: Active and disabled links
items.description: The current page is highlighted in brand color, while links to features not yet available are dimmed and non-clickable.

items.title: Responsive grid
items.description: The main content sits in a centered, max-width grid that adapts from mobile up, with the sidebar collapsing to an overlay on small screens.

blocks.title: How scrolling behaves
body: In wide, overflowing containers like card rows and spreadsheet-style tables, you can middle-click and drag to scroll horizontally, with edge indicators showing there is more to see.

When the app shell mounts it locks window-level scrolling so the sidebar and main area stay put, and it restores normal scrolling for marketing and sign-in pages. Opening the mobile sidebar overlay also freezes the page behind it until you close it.

items.question: Will Connex remember my active workspace?
items.answer: Yes. Your active workspace is stored in a cookie that lasts about a year, so you return to the same tenant even after restarting your browser.
